quiz.question: 1. What is the primary purpose of a vertical slice?
options: Implement every feature before testing anything
Demonstrate one complete workflow through the frontend, backend, data, and dependencies
Create an architecture diagram without code
Benchmark only the database
quiz.explanation: A vertical slice validates the entire end-to-end integration across frontend, API gateway, persistence, and external dependencies with real transactions before adding feature breadth.

quiz.question: 2. Why should an accepted interview answer be persisted before relying on AI evaluation completion?
options: AI inference is always instantaneous
It avoids all database transactions
It protects user work when inference fails or times out
It makes authorization unnecessary
quiz.explanation: External AI models are slow and prone to network timeouts or rate limits. Persisting the answer durably first ensures candidate work is never lost, allowing asynchronous or retried evaluation.

quiz.question: 3. What does p95 latency tell you?
options: The average amount of stored data
The time within which approximately 95% of measured requests complete or fall below, according to the metric definition
The maximum possible server latency
The number of failed database writes
quiz.explanation: Percentile latency (p95) measures tail performance: 95% of requests experience latency at or below this threshold, highlighting tail spikes that arithmetic averages completely conceal.

quiz.question: 4. When should a breakpoint test be run?
options: Against any production endpoint without permission
Before the test script has been validated
In a controlled environment with stop conditions to identify capacity limits
Only after disabling monitoring
quiz.explanation: Breakpoint testing increases load in controlled stages within an isolated test environment with predefined stop conditions to discover the exact saturation point of the first failing component.

quiz.question: 5. A worker crashes after saving a report but before sending a notification. What is a suitable design?
options: Delete the report because the notification failed
Use recoverable event processing and idempotent notification handling
Make the report depend on an active browser connection
Retry every request indefinitely
quiz.explanation: Decoupled event processing (via an Outbox pattern or message broker visibility timeout) allows another worker to retry notification dispatch idempotently without corrupting the completed report.

quiz.question: 6. What should happen when a user requests another tenant's report by changing its ID?
options: Return it if the ID is valid
Check only whether the user is logged in
Rely on the frontend to hide the report link
Enforce resource and tenant authorization on the backend
quiz.explanation: Never trust client-supplied IDs. The backend must enforce server-side ownership and organization tenant boundaries, returning HTTP 403 Forbidden on cross-tenant ID tampering (BOLA/IDOR prevention).

quiz.question: 7. How do you demonstrate that an optimization improved performance?
options: Compare reproducible benchmark results under the same defined workload
Assume it is faster because it uses a cache
Count the number of services added
Rely on a single successful request
quiz.explanation: Performance optimization claims must be supported by empirical evidence: running the exact same benchmark workload before and after the change and comparing p95/p99 latency, error rate, and throughput.

quiz.question: 8. What is a central goal of a technical defense?
options: Claim the system has no limitations
Use the largest possible technology stack
Explain and defend choices using requirements, trade-offs, and evidence
Avoid discussing failed experiments
quiz.explanation: An architectural defense demonstrates engineering maturity: justifying decisions with explicit requirements, empirical benchmark data, reasoned trade-offs, and an honest discussion of known limitations.
